course.title: BitsByBlocks · AI Engineering Notebook
course.subtitle: From zero to building and training real models — one hands-on lab, one honest Turn, and one shareable story at a time.
course.author: Ashwin Yardi

levels.name: Ground floor
levels.after: You can call an LLM on purpose instead of by vibes.

levels.name: Inside the box
levels.after: You can explain what happens to one token, end to end.

levels.name: AI engineer
levels.after: You can ship a feature on top of a model and prove it works.

levels.name: Adapter
levels.after: You can change a model's behaviour with data, not just prompts.

levels.name: Operator
levels.after: You can run it in production, fast, cheap, and observable.

levels.name: Builder
levels.after: You can reason about training and systems the way a lab does.

modules.title: What an LLM actually is
modules.question: What is the model really doing when it answers you?
modules.can: Describe an LLM as a next-token predictor, and say what that rules out.

sources.name: Karpathy, Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
Raschka, Build an LLM from Scratch, ch.1

modules.exercise: Call any chat API with the same prompt five times at temperature 1 and diff the answers.

grid: top five candidate tokens with probabilities

modules.title: Tokens: how your text becomes numbers
modules.question: Why does the model see 'strawberry' as pieces and miscount its letters?
modules.can: Predict token counts, estimate cost, and debug tokenizer weirdness.

sources.name: Karpathy, Let's build the GPT Tokenizer

modules.exercise: Tokenise ten strings with tiktoken, including an emoji, a URL, and Hindi text. Count tokens per character.

modules.question: How can a machine tell that 'doctor' and 'nurse' are neighbours?
modules.can: Explain vector similarity and pick an embedding model for a task.

sources.name: Raschka, Build an LLM from Scratch, ch.2

modules.exercise: Embed twenty sentences, compute cosine similarity, and find the pair the model thinks is closest.

flow: text to embedding to nearest neighbour

modules.title: The context window is your whole memory
modules.question: Where does the model keep what you told it two messages ago?
modules.can: Budget a prompt and explain why a long document gets ignored in the middle.

modules.title: Temperature, top-p, and why answers vary
modules.question: Why does the same prompt give a different answer each time?
modules.can: Choose decoding settings deliberately instead of copying defaults.
modules.exercise: Generate the same completion at temperature 0, 0.7, and 1.4, ten times each, and count unique outputs.

modules.question: What is actually sent over the wire when you call a chat model?

modules.title: What a call costs and why it feels slow

modules.can: Estimate cost and latency for a feature before you build it.

modules.title: Why models make things up

modules.title: Tokenizer traps that break real features

modules.title: Prompting that survives production
modules.question: Why does a prompt that worked in the playground fail on real users?

modules.title: How to evaluate something with no right answer
modules.question: The output is a paragraph, so what exactly do you measure?
modules.can: Pick a metric that moves when quality moves, and know its blind spots.

modules.exercise: Score 30 outputs yourself, then with an LLM judge, and measure how often they disagree.

modules.title: Building the eval set for your own feature
modules.question: How do you know a prompt change made things better, not just different?
modules.can: Build a small labelled set and run it on every change.

modules.title: Retrieval augmented generation, the honest version
modules.question: How do you make a model answer from your documents, not its memory?
modules.can: Build a retrieval pipeline and explain where it usually fails.

modules.title: Chunking and vector search, where RAG actually breaks
modules.question: Why did retrieval return the wrong paragraph of the right document?

figures: grid: one document cut three ways
flow: query to candidates to top-k

modules.title: Reranking and hybrid retrieval
modules.question: Embeddings return plausible chunks, so how do you get the right one on top?
modules.can: Add keyword search and a reranker, and know what each fixes.
modules.exercise: Add BM25 next to your vector search and measure precision at 3 on the same 20 questions.
figures: flow: two retrievers merging into a reranker

modules.title: Tool calling: letting the model touch your system
